newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ plans NZ$1.8 bln debt programme, 2009 benchmark.
newsitem.headline: NZ plans NZ$1.8 bln debt programme, 2009 benchmark.

text.p: The New Zealand Debt Management Office said on Thursday the 1997/98 bond tender programme would be worth a total of NZ$1.8 billion.
The programme includes $1.5 billion of nominal bonds and $300 million of inflation-indexed bonds.

The DMO proposed introducing a new 10-year benchmark bond with a maturity of July 15, 2009, in the first tender next year. The conventional bond tenders will kick off with one tender of $300 million on July 10, to be followed by eight tenders of $150 million each.
In addition, the DMO proposed holding six inflation-indexed bond tenders of NZ$50 million each during the year, beginning on August 21.
The DMO said there will be one more tender of the 2001 bond in 1997/98.
The coupon for the new 10-year bond and the mix of the bonds to be offered in the first tender will be announced on July 3.

A break-down of the 1997/98 domestic borrowing requirement showed NZ$1.843 billion of domestic debt maturing in the year, comprising $1.558 billion of government bonds in the market and $285 million of other debt repayments, including the DFC, ECNZ,

A total of $408 million was needed for repayment of foreign currency borrowing, to be financed by selling foreign currency investments. The DMO expected to receive NZ$498 million net cashflow from operatings and investing activities.
